title: Permissive licensing for publishable service crates
scope: Local package inventory and file placement. No registry lookup, archive creation or publication ran; this is not a legal-compatibility determination.

implemented.permissive_crates: Every MIT OR Apache-2.0 package directory under services/ now carries LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE and a README stating what the crate is, its dual licence and the standard contribution paragraph.
implemented.agpl_crate: services/nostr-pod-bridge keeps AGPL-3.0-only, with a full LICENSE text and a README that states it is NOT dual-licensed, so nobody publishes it under the permissive assumption.
implemented.notice: services/LICENSING-NOTICE.md and docs/developer/licensing.md updated to the actual per-directory state.
implemented.gate: scripts/ci/check-crate-licensing.sh fails if any services/ package directory lacks the texts and README its manifest declares; wired into .github/workflows/invariants.yml as an appended step.
implemented.crate_docs_match_code: services/dream-engine/README.md gained an Acceptance path section describing the seven acceptance modules (manifest, readiness, candidate, receipts, gate, runstate, roster), the veto-class to verdict mapping (harness -> BLOCKED-ENV, evidence -> REJECT, unproven -> INCONCLUSIVE), the draft-PR-only-on-gate-upheld-ACCEPT rule, and both evaluatorEntrypoints forms with the fail-closed bare-string reading. Documentation only; no Rust source was touched.

tests.stdout_tail: OK (check-crate-licensing): 8 services/ package directories carry the texts they declare.

limitations: Metadata and file placement only. No packaged-archive inspection, no registry lookup, no publication, and no maintainer review of the distribution-specific dependency/licensing position. Extracted-repository and consumed Nix revisions are unverified.
